chapters.title: The tower
chapters.say: This is Claude Tower on Robinhood Chain. Fifty floors, one automated research desk each. The house desk sits upstairs on floor fifty, and it publishes the coins it would trade.

chapters.title: Lease a floor
chapters.say: Pick any vacant floor. Here is what it costs, one floor per wallet. Beside it is the house bot's real record, kept with the house's own money.

chapters.title: Watch HQ live
chapters.say: Watch H Q live. The house floor is open to everyone, with no sign-in needed.

chapters.title: The Overview
chapters.say: The Overview. The bot's profit and loss out of its own journal, what it holds right now, and every closed trade drawn as a bar from the stop to the target.

chapters.title: The calls
chapters.say: Calls. Everything the desk published, each with an entry, a stop and a target. These are the calls your bot takes.

chapters.title: WALL-ST-E
chapters.say: Wall Street E is the bot. Your own machine, your own key, your own caps. This chain charges a flat six hundred and sixty one thousand gas for a round trip, whatever the size, so the position is what decides whether a trade can pay for itself. The measured cheapest clip is eleven point two thousandths of an E T H, and that is the default.

chapters.title: Your track
chapters.say: Team. The sixteen analysts and the boss who work this floor. On a floor you lease, this tab is also where you choose who runs your bot: yourself, with one command, and the key made on your own machine.

chapters.title: The board
chapters.say: And on the wall, the board keeps the live book, redrawn every ten seconds.

chapters.title: Plug in
chapters.say: Lease a floor. Plug in. Let it work.
